The immediate consequence for the player, manning a Thunderbolt jet fighter, is that he has to fight his way through enemies from different decades.

The game is a horizontally scrolling shooter with the basic promise of flying from left to right without getting destroyed. Helpful are the two weapon systems: the unlimited standard attack and a special attack which causes every enemy on the screen to die. Every hit and touch with the environment causes the players fuel reserve to decrease. The latter is important because there are many structures which can only be passed with precise positioning.

Published in Italy by Sovox as Power Jet.

172240.overview:
A turn-based war game set in World War II that simulates a what-if battle between General Patton and Field Marshal Rommel for control of Normandy, hence the name.

As the war is fought you get points, and the objective, of course is to gather as much points as possible (positive points if you're Allied, negative if you're Axis). Although it's strategical simulation is rather simplistic, taking a more entertaining approach, it has many features, available options and a lot of feedback from the computer (including tips from the computerized Patton's and Rommel's).

The game had a feature very similar to today's well-known Fog-of-War, though it's functionality was not as smooth as it is today. The warzone is divided into Zones of Control, with it's units and actions invisible to the adversary until he attempts to move through it and fight for it.

172241.overview: Pay Day is a 2 - 4 player board game based upon the original 1975 board game by Parker Brothers. Players take turns moving on a board shaped like a calendar of the days of the month. The goal is to have the most amount of money at the end of the game. Each person starts with $325, and players take turns rolling a single die, and move the corresponding number of positions on the board. The player chooses the number of months they wish to play each game, from 1 - 12 months. Different spaces include bills, the option to buy insurance, collect inheritance, and receive payday. At the end of each month, the player must pay their bills, and if the player's bills outweigh their payday, the player will have to take out a loan at the end of the month. There is a 20% interest each month on outstanding loans. The player can also start a savings account, where they will receive a 10% interest at the end of each month. There are special deal cards, where the player can buy unique items, and if they can find a buyer for the item, they receive a profit on the sale. Sundays are always rest days.

172243.overview: An arcade collect-em-up published in Game On 1991/02.  Explore the alien planet gathering robot parts and keeping up your energy reserves. You can use your laser blaster to kill the fiends but it will tap your much needed energy.

172337.overview: the first version of Microchess was published in 1977 for various CP/M and Z80 machines and was ported to the Commodore PET/CBM a year later. So the first version of PETChess for the C64 was pretty much ready to run even before the machine debuted. This updated game is a graphically improved, and faster version of that first port and it does a pretty good job, without too many slowdown, especially when run from floppy.

172390.overview: The Milky Weigh is an action game, published by Argus Press Software, which was released in 1983.  The reconnaissance probe sent to the distant planet Astral 4 is on its way to return to Earth and provide all the information gathered during its search. But to refuel it will have to stop on one of the various planets it encounters from time to time. Retrieve the barrel of petrol using skillful use of the engines to oppose the different forces of gravitation and then enter the black hole to continue the journey. Be careful, because as you go through your journey the difficulties will increase and you will need your skills and alertness more and more. Released as part of "30 Games" game pack.

173329.overview: This is a Boulder Dash clone, where players has to collect a number of diamonds before time runs out. Boulders (or “rockstones”, as the game describes them) scattered throughout each room can be used to the player's advantage. Removing the earth in which boulders rest cause these boulders to fall down until they hit the next piece of earth, creating a path in which the player can navigate to other areas by. Also, boulders can be used to crush any pumpkins and ghosts that are nearby. Other obstacles include changers and destructible walls. Changers create diamonds if boulders are placed on top of them, and destructible walls need to be destroyed in order to access passages that were previously sealed. Once players collect the last required diamond, they can proceed to the next room where more diamonds await them. Published in 64'er 1993/07 and 64'er 1996/08.

173332.overview: Published in the German magazine, 64'er 1997/07, this is a weird variation on the normal collect-em-up type games as the baddies seem to have certain routes they take and you just need to avoid them and gather all the dots to get to the next level.

173337.overview: An interesting cross between Load Runner and Pac-Man.

173338.overview: The sequel to the original mix between Load Runner and Pac-Man.

173339.overview: Published in 64'er 1984/08, this is one of the many Pac-Man clones with fruit, ice-cream and what might be the Torah available to collect.

173340.overview: One of the better Pacman clones that I've seen, more variety gameplay-wise. You get four difficulty levels (I started on Beginner) and a generous amount of lives (25 to start). Published in 64'er Sonderheft 97.

173344.overview: A homebrew version of Pacman where the playfield is on it's side.

173346.overview: One morning Paddington was in the garden testing some tricks from his conjuring outfit when he came across one he hadn't noticed before. It was called MAGIC DISAPPEARING INK and it looked very interesting indeed. There were three bottles inside the box. There was a black bottle which was full of everlasting ink that never disappeared; a red one containing some special ink which vanished soon after you had put it on; and a green bottle full of liquid which you brushed on to bring the words back again. It sounded very good value.

173347.overview: Paddles is a Pong variant for up to two players. The player should catch the ball when it comes towards his side. Catching the ball is rewarded with some amount of points, depending on ball speed. The bounced ball returns to the opponent's side. In the middle of the screen, it is a flashing bolt-figure, called an energy field. Every time the ball affects this, it will change its direction and speed, according to the shape of the field.

173348.overview: A single-playerTron\Worm game that is part of "Crazy Corners" and "Arcade Action" game pack.

173379.overview: A memory matching game created by Octabits and published in Game On 1993/11.

173381.overview: Players pilot a spaceship through space inhabited by aliens, and below the spacecraft is terrain where several human prisoners resides. The aliens, who also shoot projectiles at the player, make their way toward the terrain and attempt to kidnap the prisoners by taking them to the top then killing them. The player must prevent this from happening by shooting the aliens down and catching the falling prisoner with their spaceship. If the player fails to catch prisoners before they reach the terrain, that prisoner will be killed. Like Defender, players need to keep an eye on both the action and the map at the top of the screen, so that they can avoid any dangers approaching them. As well as lasers which the player can use to kill aliens, smart bombs can be activated, wiping all aliens in sight. Once all humans have been saved and all aliens killed, the player proceeds to the next wave where new aliens are introduced and the difficulty level is increased. If the player comes into contact with any of the aliens or their projectiles, the player loses a life. If the player has no lives left, the game is over.

173382.overview:
A beautiful pancake managed to escape, after being prepared and baked, from the house where so many children were ready to eat it. Now he has decided to roam around the world in search of all those good fruits that manage to enhance it and hops here and there to grab them as the birds make them fall. But the pitfalls and dangers for our cake are really many: hens, chicks the towering men will try to grab it and eat it. But if our cake is really clever, it can also grab the items the birds drop for additional points based on how many were collected. Will you be able to guide the cake and help it survive?

Published as Urca in Italy in Hit Parade C64 n.48 (Settembre 1990) and New Special PlayGames n.32 (giugno 1990).

173427.overview:
A Q-bert style action puzzle game that was part of the French "3 Super Jeux" game pack. Inspired by the arcade game Q*Bert, you take the role of Pancho who has to paint all the squares on various heights in a isometric view on a single screen. To paint a square, all Pancho has to do is land on a square but needs to avoid a Mad Mexican Muncher that moves around the screen and if he touches it then he loses one of three lives. Also moving around the screen is a wild jumping bean that changes the squares back to their original colour but this can be caught to remove it.

Pancho starts a level on one of two magic carpets and these can be stood on to have a breather as the Muncher can't land on them. Pressing the fire button anywhere on the screen transports Pancho on to one but this can only be done four times. Once the level has been cleared then it's onto the next one but with more Munchers and the squares have to be landed on more than once to paint them.

173433.overview: An arcade maze game from Dutch publishers Courbois Software from 1983 that played on the popularity of an entirely different game called Pengo.

173436.overview:
Like the TRS-80 Release of this game, Panic Button involved one working on a multi-level manufacturing line, trying to keep up orders by assembling various products. The parts drop out of 3 chutes on the top left of the playfield, and you can run all over the place to pick up the 3 different parts of the product, and you have to assemble them in order (for example, a robot must have it's feet on the bottom, torso in the middle, and head on the top). The pieces come out of the first conveyor belt in random order, and you can only carry one piece at a time. If you accidentally assemble a product in the wrong order, it becomes useless, so you have to be careful where you drop the pieces. There is also a Panic Button (hence the game name) in the upper right corner that you can hit that stops the conveyor belts temporarily.

For each level, you have to make a specific amount of the product you are creating within a time limit of 2 minutes, and each successive level gets faster and faster (and you also have to build more and more). Also, since the 3 conveyor belts are staggered, and pieces will drop on their own between them, you have to be careful watching them as they get near a drop point, as they could fall on pieces you have already constructed and potentially screw that particular product up. On later levels, the bad products start bouncing around as well, interfering with your manoeuvring.

173476.overview: A breakout style game from The Digital Underground and published in Violation #2.

173477.overview: You must find the president of Paranoids Anonymous. This is one of our most delightful adventures. You are invited to the weekly meeting of paranoids anonymous but, of course, they won't tell you where it is, or how to get in. It all makes perfect sense, if you remember the particular brand of nut you're dealing with.

173494.overview: A puzzle brain game created by Frank Ewald and published in Game On 1991/05. In this game you slide and drop pieces in order to match them, which removes them from play, freeing up other combinations. All this must be done without blocking yourself.

173495.overview: You start the game stark naked in a red, Parisian bedroom and believe it or not, things are going to get wilder from here. Parisian Nights is set between the two world wars. As Monsieur Phillip Groucy, a French Secret Service Agent, you awake in a seedy suburb of Paris with no money. You must recover your stolen credit card and maintain the health of your body and soul.

173497.overview: A fun to play horizontally scrolling shoot'em-up game, with waves and power-ups, mini-boss and bossfights and everything you expect in a good SHMUP created by X-ample Architectures and published in Game On 1993/10. This game was dedicated as such: Memorial: In honor of Commander. The brave defender of the Parsec Planets and to Kenor of 688, may your snapshots always find their target. Somewhere in a distant galaxy in the year 4096, in the observatory of a strange race, a scientist realized that something dangerous will happen. Our world will soon collide with the Uridian planet and it is your task to mobilize the strike force to destroy it before that can happen.

173507.overview:
Pallida Luna is a 1985 Italian action game developed by Enrico Meloni and published by CESE s.r.l. as a part of Amico Bit # 3

It was re-released in English in 1987 under the name Pale Moon by Systems Editoriale s.r.l. as part of Commodore 64 Club #03

Simplistic but somewhat charming oldie where you're a demented tightrope-walker who has taken it upon himself to travel across the telephone wires connecting tall buildings in search of gold that gives you more time (didn't discover this until Round 6) whilst avoiding flying boots, snake-charmers, falling plant-pots, and electrical charges.

If you fall, you scream and land up in the water below, much to the amusement of the alleycats nearby.

I used save states to get me through it quicker as you go right back to screen 1 at each drop. You can continue on each Round after losing all three of your lives.

Each Round has 6 screens. It seems to go on forever so I quit at Round 8.

This game has a similar atmosphere to On The Tiles, with the twilight blue sky and lit windows of the buildings in the background.

173586.overview: The Emperor is dead and the Parthian Empire is in chaos. Every city state in the empire has declared independence as their Kings prepare to crush all opposition and be proclaimed Emperor. You as a King command an army, hire mercenaries,make alliances and levy taxes. Your strategy, tactics and leadership will gain you an empire. City states that you have conquered must be held as you make your thrust towards final victory.Up to 4 players can play at any one time or you can play against the computer as any or all your opponents.

173587.overview:
Up to four players or teams can compete in this 2,500-question trivia game. The box includes four hand-held quick response controllers attached to four-foot cables; there is no need for players to crowd around one keyboard. You can choose the length of the game, the number of players (one to four), and the time allowed to answer a question. You can also handicap advanced players.

Media for Commodore 64 and Apple II/Atari 8-Bit computers is included in the one box.

Questions comprise of general knowledge, history, music, math pop culture and American television.

Additional Question Disks Sold Seperately Include:
General Edition 2
Entertainment Edition 1
Sports Edition 1

173588.overview: A comprehensive education and driving quiz game for the UK circa 1987. There are 40 lessons, each of which deals with an important topic that is likely to arise in the written portion of your test.

173589.overview: Passengers on the Wind II allows players to decide the fate of the heroes and direct all of them so that they reach their aim. Players will discover many locations, directions, and events; and will live different stories according to the directions that he makes the characters take. Everything is controlled using either the keyboard or the joystick. Players are both the director and the heroes. The screen is divided into three main elements: a graphical section where the action takes place; a section showing the character players are directing; and the section containing text, from which players decide the action. The player can take several actions during the game: saving a game, viewing flashbacks (in slow or fast motion), or intervention on the central graphic screen to make the action develop. The game is split into seven episodes which players have to gradually make their way through. In each, a main scene is displayed in the graphical section, and by simple confirmation players can make the characters appear. To avoid restarting the game at the beginning each time, players are given an opportunity to save the situation in progress. In this case, a blank, formatted disk is required to save these situations.

173590.overview: Passport to London is a maze and strategy game. Welcome to London. You are a tour guide in charge of 12 very enthusiastic tourists. Alas, your your tourists have two nasty habits. They tend to wander off and get lost, and they like to take home 'souvenirs' of priceless British treasures. Your mission is to track down the missing objects. The player must investigate 9 separate tourist sites in London. Each location contains a maze of tourists, and the player must locate the tourists and bobbies in each location. They will give information on which tourist may have stolen which item. Of note, tourists will move between locations every 15 - 30 minutes. Once the player has determined which tourist has stolen which item, they must be tracked down, and accused of which item they stole and where they stole it from. The player will occasionally encounter ghosts, who randomly transport the player to a different location. The player has 100 pounds and 12 hours to find the missing items. The player can travel by bus, taxi, underground, or walking. All 4 options use a different amount of time and money. The game is over when the player has run out of money or time, or has collected all missing items.

173591.overview: Passport to Paris is an arcade and strategy game. Welcome to Paris. You are a tour guide in charge of 12 very enthusiastic tourists. Unfortunately, you have just received a message that their flight will be leaving an hour earlier than scheduled. You need to track down all 12 tourists, or be responsible for them missing their return flight. The player must investigate 6 separate tourist sites in Paris. Each location contains a mini-game, and the player must locate the tourists and their names in each section. They player will also receive clues as to where each tourist is located. Mini-game sections include: navigating the lines of tourists at the Louvre, lighting candles at the Notre Dame, talking to waiters at the Moulin Rouge, listening to music at the opera, talking to artists at Montmarte, and finding tourists at the Eiffel Tower. The player has 200 francs and 12 hours to find the missing items. The player can travel by bus, taxi, metro, or walking. All 4 options use a different amount of time and money. The game is over when the player has run out of money or time, or has collected all missing items.

173837.overview:
Psytronik Software presents PRECINCT 20:Dead Strange, a beautifully crafted new release for the Commodore 64 from accomplished game designer Alf Yngve, based on his novel by the same name.  In this incredibly atmospheric horror-themed game you must solve a series of ritual murders carried out by an evil cult.
 
Featuring moody noir-esque graphics, genuinely unsettling gameplay (you never know what is going to jump out of the shadows at you!) superb music by Richard Bayliss that really sets the scene - complete with screams and eerie heartbeats, this is possibly Alf's finest release to date!


He's detective Innis Garris, Homicide Squad, Precinct 20. Garris gets all the weird cases. 
 Now he's chasing several mysterious killers...  A cult called "The Sons of Albhukra" has committed a string of ritual murders.  A figure called "The Birdman" slays people... and pecks out the eyes of his victims.  A stalker only known as "Slenderman" preys on lonely pedestrians.
 
There are rumors that these killers may not even be human. There are strange sightings of a giant terrifying face. Down these dark streets one man must walk.

173912.overview:
A solitaire variant published in Magic Disk 64 1989/12. 

Patience games typically involve dealing cards from a shuffled deck into a prescribed arrangement on a tabletop, from which the player attempts to reorder the deck by suit and rank through a series of moves transferring cards from one place to another under prescribed restrictions. Some games allow for the reshuffling of the decks, or the placement of cards into new or "empty" locations. In the most familiar, general form of patience, the object of the game is to build up four blocks of cards going from ace to king in each suit, taking cards from the layout if they appear on the table.

173913.overview: As Polly, your task is to turn over a series of cards until it matches the one the game asks for. To turn a card over, you must highlight the card by walking underneath the bottom of it, and pressing the fire button. Depending on the number of screens you specify at the start of the game, a total of 52 cards can be in play. Some cards can reveal jokers that chase Polly around the screen, and these jokers must be avoided. If a joker catches Polly, then she goes back to the start of the current screen. Three levels, which can also be specified at the start, determine how difficult the game becomes. If neither the number of screens or the level is selected, a self-running demo shows you what you have to do, and this demo runs until Polly comes into contact with a joker.

173914.overview: A computerized version of the popular mathematical puzzle game Towers of Hanoi. This version was developed by Henrik Holmdahl and published by CP Verlag in Game On 1992/12.

173915.overview:
A SEUCK based Shoot'em-up game developed by Carsten Manshusen and published in Magic Disk 64 1988/08, and GO64! 2004/11. 

In the game "Paul the Beetle" you steer Paul through the dangerous world and accompany him on his way. Since this expedition does not always go on without losses, Paul naturally has several lives.

Everything that moves should be avoided as much as possible. To get such enemies out of the way, Once you have reached the end of a level, it will take a while before you can advance to the next level. The landscape changes and in no more time and you have to wait and be careful not to get hit by anything.

173916.overview: A collect'em-up game in which you have to collect bags of money for 1 or 2 simultaneous users, created by Niklas Bichinger and published in Game On in 1995/04.

173917.overview:
In this collect 'em up developed and published by C.P. White, you must go around in a maze collecting green peas.

Watch out for the giant pea monster (more like a green Pac-Man ghost in terms of its resemblance) or he will eat you. You can break the swinging doors by moving at the same time as the giant pea, but he will soon repair them. Eat him when he turns a nice juicy red color.

173918.overview: Peanuts Maze Marathon is a simple puzzle game designed for children 4-8. The game features characters from Charles Shulz's Peanuts who, for one reason or another, need to get from one location to their destination. In between the locations is a randomly generated maze players need to solve in order to help out the characters; once players successfully guide a dot through the maze to the exit, a short animation is shown. Players can optionally select a time limit for completing each maze; default values of 4, 3, or 2 minutes are provided, or players can enter in the number of seconds or minutes they would like.

173919.overview:
Peanuts Picture Puzzler is a Peanuts comic strip themed puzzle game for the Apple II.

The player is shown a Peanuts themed picture, which is then divided into 4 blanked out sections. The picture must choose the correct piece for each section to complete the puzzle and watch an animated vignette. The player can choose timed or untimed puzzles.

173920.overview:
This is an arcade adventure similar to Dizzy series and set in medieval fantasy world. The goal of the game is to find the pearl of dawn and to do so you'll have to explore many screens, including the castle and it's surroundings. The basic gameplay is a typical action game without platform jumping elements, however besides slaughtering or avoiding all types of enemies you also need to solve "puzzles" - pick up objects lying on the ground and then find where to use them to proceed further. Pearl of Dawn features many interconnected screens that can be freely traversed back and forth. The game features 2.5D-like-graphics - think Golden Axe, but characters can only move in two planes. 

Published in Game On 1992/06

173921.overview: A Frogger style game where you must get the pedestrian across a busy highway, then avoid the spiders and aliens then across a croc infested stream to get them safely home. Keep the pedestrian on his toes!! One wrong move and you'll wish you had driven instead.

173922.overview:
Pegasus Odyssey is an action video game released in 1983 for Commodore 64 by Comm * Data of Milford . You control a Pegasus with a mechanism similar to that of the well-known arcade Joust . The game takes place on a fixed screen showing a range of mountains, including a glowing volcano. The player's pegasus and enemies move in two dimensions across the screen, and when they leave the left side they reappear on the right side and vice versa.

The player must repeatedly press the button to make the pegasus flap its wings and gain altitude, while if you stop pressing it tends to spontaneously go down. For horizontal displacements you can accelerate and decelerate only while flapping your wings, then the movement continues indefinitely by inertia. The bottom side of the screen is the ground, on which you can land and slide horizontally. On the upper side of the screen it bounces. 

The enemies are giant bats that come out a little at a time from a cave in the mountains and fly continuously. To eliminate them, the pegasus must strike them from a higher position; on the other hand, if the bat arrives on the pegasus from above, the player loses a life . Each downed bat becomes an egg that bounces to the ground, and when it finally stops it can be made to disappear by walking over it. If, on the other hand, you lose too much time, a bat is reborn from the egg. When the pegasus is eliminated, if you still have lives, you re-enter the game when the player commands it; the volcano shoots out a fireball which then turns into the new pegasus.

Two players can participate in simultaneous cooperation, controlling two pegasi, who cannot touch each other, but pass through each other unscathed. Ten levels of difficulty are available.

173923.overview: This arcade inspired game has you playing as a penguin who must survive various mazes made of ice for two minutes to move on to the next maze. The whole of each maze is shown on the screen as you try to avoid other creatures and also try to get as many bonus points as possible within the two minutes.

173924.overview: A Pengo clone. Escape the monsters, arrange the ice blocks. You are caught in a room full of boulders where ghosts roam between. Smash the ghosts with the stones and suck up the rest of the boulders. Simple amateur version of the arcade game.

173925.overview:
Pensate is a strategy game where the player has to move his castle across a checkerboard, from the bottom to the top. The game is turn based and for each turn the player gives instructions on how the castle should move. Number of moves that can be made in a turn is decided before the start of a new game (one to four). The player can move in four directions, up, down, left and right. To reach the top the player has to avoid ten different types of enemies who move around the board at the same time as the player. They differ in the way they move around the board. The most basic enemies can move one step at a time in a specific direction, while others make the opposite move of the player. So if the player moves north, the enemy moves south. Some enemies matches the player's move but turn them a certain amount of degrees clockwise or counterclockwise. Another enemy moves like a chess knight and jumps to a non-adjacent square via an L-shaped path.

The game has two play modes; practice and tournament. In the practice mode the player creates his own selection of enemies to play against while in the tournament mode he plays pre-made levels. The tournament is round based and for each round the player faces more and tougher enemies. The game is playable by one or two players. In a two player game one player starts at the top and has to move to the bottom. Also published in Loadstar #040.

173926.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter where you guide your dragon, Peppi through a harsh cityscape avoiding and shooting the baddies as they come at you and vanquishing the boss monsters to make it to the next area.

173928.overview: Based on the arcade game Pengo, this was a game of "The Big 100" collection.

173930.overview:
An obscure puzzle game created by Axel Teichmann and published in Magic Disk 64 1992/09. 

Anyone who does not want to bargain for a complex with Perplex in the long run has to be completely at it. There are several grey and brown building blocks on a total of 64 levels. The aim of the game can perhaps be explained as follows: the grey stones are the bad guys and the brown stones are the good ones. The good now try to convert the bad, which can be put into practice by simply touching them. If all the greys have now switched to the browns' side, the next level can be tackled.

Unfortunately, the brown blocks only have a certain number of "moves" available, so each move has to be carefully considered. Fortunately, there is no time limit. To increase long-term motivation, the Password of the corresponding level specified.

173931.overview: A miscellaneous, single player arcade game created by Tuffan Production, published in Game On 1994/01 (Play Time 01/1994).

173932.overview:
Pertharion is a game that gets your grey brain cells going again, namely a mind game. The shooting friends among you should also keep reading, because the game hardly lacks excitement and thrills. Now the boy shouldn't talk so much, but go to medias res. So, let's go! You see a rotating ball on a playing field, with which you have to drive over differently coloured fields (control options: left, right, up, down, but not diagonally). These boxes have different influences on the further course of the game. But you have to stay on the box, otherwise you have unfortunately lost. The following selection of fields are available on the field:

GREEN that you can rest on, it's safe land. But there are also greens that show cracks, they disappear once you have rolled over them.

BLUE, it is no longer possible to change direction here. H. the ball moves as if on ice to the next differently coloured field. So it can happen that at the end of the ice field there is no more box and you go on it without being able to do anything about it. Usually they remain, but if you come across a blue field with cracks, it disappears again. What a pity! ! !

A little friendlier are the VIOLETS, which flash and which you have to collect in every level. Unfortunately, they move away after rolling over once. So you have to take care that you don't suddenly stand there and only the black background surrounds you, cut off from the environment, lonely on a small island. Because then it's unfortunately GAME OVER! ! ! ! !

Another complication is that you only have one life at your disposal. So think first before you take the next step. You mustn't stand on a box that disappears when touched (all with cracks and purple), because otherwise you can make your will very quickly.
The control of the ball takes a little getting used to, but you are quite used to it and after a night session you master the control, but the game is far from exhausted.

Because there is also the possibility to create or change your own or existing levels, namely 989 pieces.

Created by Jürgen Graser and published in Magic Disk 64 1991/09.

173933.overview:
PET Checkers allows the player to play checkers against the computer. The standard international rules apply: taking turns the player may move any piece one tile diagonally as long as that tile is free. Normal pieces can only move towards the other player, but once a piece reaches the other side of the board, it is crowned and can from then on move in both directions. Pieces can be hit by being jumped over. The first player to lose all pieces loses the game.

The game keeps track of the time and uses field number input to determine moves.

This game was originally created for the Commodore PET computer, but as it could also be run on later Commodore Machines, they were some of the first games available for the new platform.

173934.overview: Nuclear Power Plant is a simulation game in which the player is in control of a nuclear power plant. The goal is to make energy without letting things run out of control. Each day in the game the player can set the position of the control rods and determine the flow of various cooling systems. The next day the player gets to see the fruit of his or her labors and try to improve on (or fix) the actions of the previous day. There are many variables the player must bear in mind such as turbine capacity, coolant levels, maintenance, extreme temperatures and possible meltdown.

173935.overview: A chess game that uses PETSCII symbols and text only to allow the chess logic the largest amount of memory\processing speed to go towards the chess move calculations rather than fancy graphics.

173965.overview:
As secret agent Rupert Pettigrew, your task is to track down five other agents as well as the famed Safras sword.

In four parts:
The Searching - The Returning - The Discovery - The Conclusion.

This is in part a compilation of Shard's two games Pettigrew's Diary and Operation Safras. Published in 64 Tape Computing Ekstranr. 2.

173966.overview:
In this game you have to stack polygons that rain down from the top in the most orderly way possible, matching the faces exactly  and not leaving many spaces between one piece and another. If a horizontal line has no spaces then it will disappear bringing the tower of pieces lower and giving you more time to think. Finish the game when your castle reaches the top of the screen. If you fill in 150 lines you go to the next level: if you fill 3, 4 or 5 in a row you have bonus pieces to fill in the gabs that have formed. You can meditate on which position to put the piece and see the piece that will be the next in line at the top left. You can play alone or with a friend in alternating fashion or in a random pattern if you so choose at the beginning. Pressing fire rotates the pieces as they fall and if you push down the move faster. Happy puzzling. 

Published in SYS PD Diskett#43 (1993) and in Italy as Fadrika in Super C64 e C128 n.40 (dicembre 1989) and in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - 30 fantastici games (1990).

173967.overview: This is a short game with some quite weird puzzles, particularly the final one. You must find the way to the princess so that she can rescue you. Turnabout, is fair play.

173999.overview: A Skramble style game except without any shooting, this game focuses entirely on the Avoid-it part of the game where you try not to get hit by the dozens of vertically shooting missiles and gain score by progressing safely.

174000.overview: An Egyptian themed multi-screen platform game published in Game On 1992/09 that uses some of the sprites from Myth.

174016.overview: A shoot'em up game of the "Cassette 50" collection. Fire your phaser at the attacking waves that descend down the screen.

174017.overview:
Philippic is a logical/brain/puzzle game created in Axel Teichmann and published in Magic Disk 64 1992/12. 

The playing field consists of four test tubes, each of which has three different colors. The aim of the game is to transfer the given color combination (lamps above the lower box) onto the lower color box by cleverly stacking them. 

With the joystick in port # 2 you control a drawer with two compartments, which logically also contains two colors. By pressing the fire button, the paint is sucked out of the compartments and placed on top of the corresponding pile. At the same time, the drawer fills up again with the colors from the bottom two compartments. That sounds more or less simple now, but it isn't! Between the top and bottom stones there are six other colored compartments that only become visible when you start your way down. As soon as the color of the lamps matches the colors of the lowest compartments, the level is over and 1000 bonus points are guaranteed.

174018.overview: A crosshairs shooter by Patriot Games and released into the public domain 1996. The point of the game is to shoot as many of the Psychoballs as possible in one minute. Race your pals and see who is quickest!

174019.overview: These Physics tests a collection of multiple choice questions designed to exercise the student who is preparing for the GCE examinations. The questions are selected randomly from the file and offered continuously until ) is entered in reply to a question whereupon you will be presented with your score.

174041.overview:
Picture Kingdom is a version of Hamurabi with some simple graphics. The gameplay is completely identical. Like in the original the game is played in turns and each turn the player must select:
How many acres of land to buy or sell
How many bushels of grain to feed to his people
How many bushels of grain to plant
Various random events will try to throw the player of course in his calculations.

174060.overview: A language and word knowledge educational game for young children from ShareData that was released as part of "Children's Collection" game pack in 1987. It is designed to help increase vocabulary in an adaptive storytelling environment.

174061.overview: A brain logic game created in 1996 by Özden Irmak & Mert Hekimci along with Timo Buschmann graphics and Balázs Bócsa for music\sound. Match the like pieces, but be careful to get all the like ones in pairs or at one time. A stranded shape will halt the game. Simply put like pieces side by side to remove them.

174062.overview: A game inspired by Dr. Mario and published in 64'er 1994/12. a hot game about pills and germs! Reaction and combination skills are in demand. Dexterity and a bit of strategy are required to hunt down insidious viruses with pills in our game. The game "Pill-Box" is based on a Tetris-like principle and also creates similarly long game sessions in front of the monitor.

174064.overview: This game is particularly simple, as it consists of a pinball game that involves the use of a single button, the space bar. The main purpose consists of shooting the ball so that it goes into all 9 bins (numbered 111 through 999) in only 15 tries. The duration you hold the space bar increases the power at which the ball is ejected into the playing field. Luck plays an important role in this simple recreation of early pinball games.

174066.overview: A pong style game released by S+S Soft Vertriebs GmbH and by Digital Marketing PD #234.

174067.overview:
An "Oil's Well" clone created by Jörg Sieslack and published in Magic Disk 64 1990/12.

From the tunnel entrance, the pipeline can be moved along the aisles using a joystick, collecting the many oil points. When the fire button is pressed, the pipeline is brought in piece by piece, i.e. it moves back towards the conveyor tower as long as the joystick button is held down.

Danger looms from the elements already mentioned that cross the underground tunnel system. If such an object moves towards the pipeline and touches it, a life is forfeited.

So it is advisable to eat the villains before contact. Of course, this only works with the head of the pipeline. You should (as is actually the case in our culture, unless you eat at McDonald 's) take your time as the pipeline also wants to digest the boys. If you refrain from lingering briefly on the spot, it can well happen that an overload will paralyze the device. Aim to collect all oil points on the field.

The player also plays against the clock. If this has dropped to 50 units, the upper area of ​​the shaft is refilled with oil points. The time limit increases slightly when a blinking object is eaten. All in all, it is important to vacuum 6 tunnel systems. A pipeline is lost if one of the villains touches it, a villain is eaten too quickly, or the time is up.

174107.overview: Published in the game compilation, Bits, Pieces and Clues and also in the Interactive Adventures Game Pack.

174108.overview:
Hi diddlely dee, a pirate's life for me. A platform based shooter published in New Special Playgames N°09 (Maggio 1988) supplement: Games Commodore 64 N°1.

Let's enter the world of ships and pirate raids with this game that sees you as a protagonist in the role of Alberto. His task is to rescue his girlfriend who has been imprisoned in one of the cabins on the vessel of the cruel pirate Black John. Monsters, witches, cannonballs and goblins will hinder your mission. Here are some tricks that will be very useful in the game: on the stern ladder and on the cords of the trees: avoid any hostile figure and defend yourself by shooting, so your hands are busy to keep you clinging to the ladder you can only shot to the right. On the deck  go down the stairs by tilting the joystick 45 degrees downwards/right. After passing the two masts of the ship you'll be able to go below deck using the ladder. You can enter the various rooms there by placing Alberto in front of the door. He will turn towards the door, now you hit the button to enter. Hidden below is a magical terminal of the future that once touched will inform you if you have completed the search in all the cabins, if so it will bestow a key. This key will open the door of the cabin where your beloved is held.

174110.overview: Pizza is a simple game in which the player must deliver pizzas to earn money. The player can choose how many pizzas he or she must deliver. Once started the player will receive orders and must point the driver to the right location on the grid, by giving the coordinates of the final address as marked on the map. If the player gives the wrong coordinate the player loses some money and must try again. There is no time limit or high-scores table.

174111.overview: A 2P Only (Simultaneous) dueling game that was part of "Combat Pack" and "2 Player Game Pack" game pack.

174113.overview:
In the year 2250, the PAO spacecraft arrived on the planet Nap, invading it entirely. After 100 years the planet has not yet been liberated and this is how the aliens are still rulers. Now it's your turn to free the planet and luckily your spaceship is greatly upgraded to take on an enemy of this scope. 

Published in Italy as Planet War in Byte Games n.33 (luglio/agosto 1989).

174115.overview:
Destroy the mini attacking planets in this simple but fun blaster from Richard Bayliss.

Released as part of Scene World #22.

174116.overview: An out of this world educational quiz about the planets in our galaxy.

174117.overview: Moon Buggy clone with a Smurf in space. Odd how your lives are labelled as ships.

174124.overview: Published in Digital Marketing PD #229 and game of the "Cassette 50" collection. You must defend your planet from a fleet of UFO's by guiding missiles to them. They accelerate as they come down to bomb your planet. You have twenty missiles to shoot down 10 of the UFOs. You can also use the hyperthrust which gives an extra burst of speed but makes the missile difficult to control. If your planet is destroyed if you run out of missiles. UFOs that escape will return.

174125.overview: A shooter that is a game of the "Cassette 50" collection. Avoid the asteroids and space mines and when the plasma bolts power up to block you, you need to shoot at the sides to allow you to proceed. Don't shoot the mines!

174126.overview:
Our program transforms you into skilled pipe-fitter by adding one shaped piece at a time, whose shape is indicated in the square at the bottom left of the screen and which indicates the shape of the piece that you can insert in your scheme. Based on your initial optional choice on the type of game you intend to play, you can adjust what you have to do and where you have to place that particular piece. The goal is to display on the screen of your computer the starting point and the ending point of the pipeline to be built. The presentation screen brings up the cursor on the left side from which the piece indicated in the center of the square located at the bottom left. Move the cursor to where you want to lay pipe. The score will depend on the length of the pipeline built. 

Published in Italy as Worker Pipes in Videoteca Computer n.38.

174127.overview: A puzzle game for one or two players. When you bounce off of the squares on the board, many of them will disintegrate, so be sure to plan your route to all the squares of your color.  When you have hit the objective number for your level, you move on to a new one. You have 3 lives and will lose them by jumping to an empty space. The game came with a built in Editor so you could create your own challenges and play them with your friends.

174128.overview: Planetfall is sci-fi business trading game. The players (game hasn't single player mode) command merchant Starfleet - they can travel between the different planetary systems (with changing business conditions), buy and sell various resources (6 - Uranium, Iron Ore, Machinery, Medical supplies, Computers and Gems), make money and collect them in banks. A game can have a maximum of 15 star-systems.

174152.overview:
Play tennis against a friend or the computer, published in Magic Disk 64 1993/09.

Wimbledon 1993. Boris Becker has once again not achieved his goal, because Pete Sampras won the final at Wimbledon. You can now pick up the racket yourself, "Play A Match" offers all the advantages of the popular tennis sport. "Play A Match" can of course also be played in pairs. If this is the case, the joystick in port # 2 controls the player at the bottom of the screen, the joystick in port # 1, of course, controls the top tennis crack. Several settings can be made in the selection menu, such as:

Joystick down - change the color of the place Joystick up - change the level Joystick right - play against computer Joystick left - play against humanoids The match is started with fire.

The normal tennis rules are played, but the second serve has been removed as it only hinders the flow of the game.
When you hit you push fire and then in the desired direction.
This should be done very quickly to avoid unnecessary points of error. If you are too slow, you simply play straight ahead.

 When the game is in full swing, a few other rules count. If the felt ball is exactly next to the player's sprite and you then press fire, the ball is hit straight ahead. The earlier or later you thrash the ball, the more obliquely it will be played. It takes a little practice.

174153.overview: A Bridge card game published with accompanying book "Bridge Puzzles Number 1" by Alfred Sheinwold. Guides you through correct play of 91 deals designed by renowned bridge teacher and authority Alfred Sheinwold.

174189.overview:
Straightforward and easy platformer, featuring that ever-popular video game character Pacman. Simply collect items for points, jump the spikes/water, dodge/kill the ghosts, and open the locks with keys to progress.

Created in 2016 by Andrea Schincaglia and Saul Cross as part of the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2015/2016.

A commercial sequel Platman Worlds was released in 2017.

174190.overview:
Platman Worlds is an exploration platformer game. You play as Platman, who bears a striking resemblance to Pacman, and need to find your way through four different worlds (Classic, Gothic, Ancient and Future). Each world consists of several screens, which contain some enemies (usually ghosts) to be avoided, keys to unlock doors and much food to collect. The screens are connected together in the world and can branch into alternate and optional paths, or require some backtracking after finding a suitable key.

This is the commercial homebrew sequel to the original Platman

174192.overview: Plazma Ball is a tactical, turn-based American Football game. Each team has 16 athletes (eleven on the field) and in each round, the player may move between zero and all of them. Other options are blocking another athlete or setting up a ball throw (if it is in possession). Before the match starts, both players also have the opportunity to set up their teams within an 50 yards radius. The outcomes of throwing attempts and fights between athletes are calculated from their statistics. The game is played within a league of four divisions (four teams each) and up to two players can take control over one team each.

174193.overview: An Arkanoid style game published originally created by Arjan Bjorn Mensch aka Ramy with 33 levels and published in Game On 1992/12 and later in Game On GE 1993/1. Two billion years ago, a vicious oppressor named Gohd trapped your friends in his fortress on the planet Gohdinia. You were chosen to find Gohdinia and to destroy the evil empire of Gohd and free your friends.

174205.overview: A horizontally scrolling spaced shoot'em up game that somewhat resembles Armalyte. It was developed by Cosmos Designs and  published in Game On 1991/12 and also in Magic Disk 64 GE 1993/2.

174206.overview:
A 2 player only , simultaneous strategy game created by Kopido Games and published in Magic Disk 64 1993/01. 

After starting the program, the screen shows an atomic lattice that can be moved with the cursor (joystick in port # 2). Each atomic nucleus has 2, 3 or 4 electrons, depending on the position of the screen. They are all colored gray (neutral). If the first player selects an atom in port # 1, it and one of the electrons turns red. Now the second player in port # 2 can select an atom with the fire button. After all, it is a matter of coloring all electrons on an atom by alternately clicking them against another player. If a fully colored plutonium is selected, it swashes over the neighboring atoms and thereby also colors opposing atoms.

The overloaded atom becomes neutral again (gray) after the explosion. By tactically placing the electrons, you can trigger chain reactions that wipe out your opponent on the field with one blow. Atoms that have already been colored can no longer be be clicked.

174207.overview: Part of the part of the "Red Ribbon Game Pak". You control Poga, your faithful remote controlled robodroid. Poga's only form of movement is bouncing. You must bounce Poga along his path in his strange mechanical world, avoiding contact with such nasties as spinning nuts and bolts, electromagnetic coils and strange flying robot birds. But all this bouncing strains Poga's mechanical parts, so you must keep him well oiled. You must control him to pick up as many oil cans as possible to increase your score.

174208.overview: Bounce around mazes fixing bricks and gathering bonuses while avoiding obstacles in Pogo Stick, a multi-level arcade style game for the 64. Fix all the bricks before the hour glass empties to go to the next level.

174209.overview: Pong but with some extra twang to make things interesting. This is a game for 2 players only. Battle against a friend in this crazy Pong remake. Make your paddles hit the ball towards your opponent's goal. It you're smart enough! The first player to score 9 points is the winner.

174249.overview: An exercise in futility. A release inspired to frustrate and anger you. The game purports to require a police security password, but it is fake and doesn't even check the input. There are indications that this was created as retribution for cracking and releasing games from Crystal Computing and was released into the wild in some of the places that were guilty of this. This is just a demo/fake game.

174250.overview:
An upgraded Worm/Snake style game published in Magic Disk 64 1994/05, Commodore Scene #21. 

The game is based on the classic "Snake", but only experts will recognize that straight away. You take on the role of the leader wolf, who asks the party guests to participate in the polonaise.

All you have to do is touch them and it is only a matter of time before the line of people fills the entire hall. If for some reason the beginning of the snake touches the end or any middle part, the polonaise dissolves in a tumult and the game is over. In addition, you must not take your time, otherwise the party guests, who are already in a bad mood anyway, will leave bored.

174252.overview: An educational game teaching numbers and patterns. Help your froggy friend move around the pond by determining the direction and number of hops to make at each step as you work your way to the farthest lilly-pad. The challenge is tough. To win, you must unlock the secret of the pond and show your frog the safe path across. You need to find the pattern that will carry the frog safely through the maze of lily pads. To find the pattern, you'll want to scout ahead from lily pad to lily pad and then test your alternate routes. Beware of blind alleys. As the frog hops from pad to pad, the risks are high. One wrong move... and splash. the frog is in the water ... and you are back at the beginning. Six levels of difficulty make this colorful program a challenge for the whole family.

174253.overview: Something that looks as close as it can to the original Atari Pong for two simultaneous players including greyscale colors. Developed by Cornal Nalla and Johan Øberg and released into the public domain in 2016.

174254.overview: A 2P Only (Simultaneous) pong style game with a twist...literally. The year of release is currently unknown.

174281.overview: A slot/fruit machine gambling game coded by Peter Gaal and Zoltán Frombach with Attila Jancsina who designed the graphics, and Péter Varga who did the SFX/music. It was published in Game On 1992/04.

174282.overview: Collect the pots on each floor. They are guarded by giant robots. Move and climb ladders, jump the shooting robots and avoid their shots.

174283.overview: Pot Panic is a puzzle game resembling a simpler version of Klax. You are the pot washer at a large restaurant. As the restaurant is extremely busy at the moment, the pots have a tendency to keep tumbling down. You have to stack the pots so that five pots of each respective type are stacked one on top of the other. As soon as you have managed this, the pots will immediately disappear and you will have space for new ones.

174286.overview: You are a German spy for the Allies. Your mission is to break into an English Prisoner of War camp and steal a set of plans. When you have escaped, deliver the plans to the resistance. You have two hours to complete your mission. Consult your watch to find out how much time you have left.

174303.overview:
A water sports game also published in o Games n.7 (March 1986) as Fuori Bordo (Or in English: Out of Edge). 
 
You are driving a powerful outboard and you have to make a route, with a certain number of laps, in a very limited time. Of course, the route has many pitfalls, which we do not reveal to you so that you can discover them yourself in the action of the moment! So, always be alert and ready to dodge.

174304.overview: Power Box Leicester & Stafford, Morning and Afternoon Shift. Set on a Summer day in the mid 1980's the simulation allows you to control traffic for two four hour shifts which we think you will find challenging as you keep traffic flowing smoothly with the minimum of delay to booked timings.

174305.overview: Power signal boxes are effective and safe form of signalling control, integral to the coordination and direction of rail yard freight engines and cars. The PSB Highlands routes have particular challenges to a rail yard manager and you need to be up to the task in this train simulation and management game from Dee-Kay systems in 1988.

174306.overview: A game, which I was too late for the 2001 Crap Game Compo, but I share this with you all. This was programmed in hardcore assembly language. The aim of the game is to guide your orb around the flashing maze and reach the exit before time runs out. If the player touches the flashing maze, it goes back to the start again. Tough, but possible to play - oh and crap as well. Well, it was meant to be crap anyway!

174307.overview:
Published as part of the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2013. 
The world's fossil resources are exhausted. Two polar subterranean thermal reactors supply the increasing energy demand of mankind. An explosion in the Northern polar thermal reactor has destroyed all primary and secondary energy connections and contact with the engineers and rescue robots has been lost.

Without an energy supply the death of billions is imminent! We need the five control diamonds to engage the station's backup systems. Use the shielded suit and the Powerglove to protect you against the maintenance robots.

Powerglove is a classic-era run 'n' gun game developed by ​Lazy​cow for the 30 year old Commodore 64 home computer, initially released as an entry in the RGCD 2013 RGCD 16K C64 Game Development Competition (where it placed 3rd out of 15 entries). This final version features a revised five level map with Powerboots and Energy Doors, faster room-change, slicker player controls, a map overview display, bug fixes, game balance tweaks and a much-requested shot sound effect!

Powerglove has full NTSC support, and the game and music run at the same speed as on PAL systems.

174308.overview: Two players join forces to outpass, outcheck and outshoot the computer team. Your shift on the ice will involve power-play opportunities, penalty killing chores and goalkeeping stick saves. Prepare to face off for bruising hockey action.

174310.overview: This game is a platform adventure game first released in 1992 in Europe under the name Powers of Gloom and developed by Michael Bacik. It was then released with slightly altered graphics in 1995 by New Entry under the name Satan Ballads. The New Entry version was converted to NTSC and published in Loadstar #151.

174311.overview:
A vertically scrolling shooter where you are the lone pilot of a spaceship, your mission is to reach the heart of the enemy attack system at the end of a narrow tunnel. This corridor is extremely dangerous as it is protected from meteorites and space vehicles of various kinds. As you maneuver to avoid obstacles, fire lasers to destroy or at least keep enemy forces away, keep the energy level constant by traversing the energy stars, and rejoin your mothership to continue the daring mission. 

Published in Italy as Corridoio Nemico in the Super Game 2000 n.6 (luglio/agosto 1985) compilation.

174312.overview:
After the sudden passing of the giant comet Blazer 76 which hit Delos V with its poisonous gases, only a group of men in sector 98 had managed to survive, albeit with difficulty. The only way out would have been to reach the spaceport in the central sector, the only way to the station. But reluctantly, the men realized that the central beacon, which alone could coordinate the course along the tangled patch of the magnetic rails or Powertrack, had failed. It will therefore be necessary for a heroic volunteer on a manually-guided shuttle to try to solve the puzzle of the intricate connection network to reach the guideposts without damage and thus allow, after having repaired it, the escape of the precarious community of Sector 98. 

Published under the name Pulse in Italy in  New Special PlayGames n.3 (novembre 1987) and in  Hit Parade C64 n.21 (Marzo 1988).

174313.overview: A one or two player Tetris clone finished on 30.03.96 by Venom Group. It has keyboard or joystick controls and high score saving feature.

174319.overview: Get your friend go head to head and protect your goal, while simultaneously trying to score. Try to get your ball into your opponents goal. First person with most points after 20 rounds wins. Goal locations and obstacles change every round. Developed by 59 Productions and published in Game On 1995/02 (Play Time 02/1995).

174320.overview:
Match shapes two of a kind of the items falling from the top. You can catch the falling items and move them to new columns. Some items have special features, match two bombs and they will remove another piece below them. If a column fills up, game over.

Published in Magic Disk 64 1995/02.

174322.overview: A political simulation of the US presidential elections, President Elect allows you to simulate any campaign from the 60's to the upcoming (at the time) 1984 election as the campaign manager for any of the candidates featured in said elections. You can also create a custom candidate by completing an RPG-like character creation module and have him/her face off against actual politicians rated in a series of stats according to their political views and ideologies. Using a series of text-based menus you can run the campaign from labor day to the election night and allocate funds, agree to debates and perform other money-raising / PR stunts in hopes of conquering as many votes as possible.

174328.overview:
A puzzle game of skill which tests your responsiveness and dexterity created by Matthias Weber and published in Magic Disk 64 1991/06. 

The basic idea of ​​PRIDE is to eliminate a number of coloured pieces and to go to the next level. Here is a somewhat more detailed explanation.

You control a ball with the joystick, with which you can and should make the coloured tokens disappear when touched.

There are three good reasons for this:

Firstly, you get points for each stone eliminated in your score account.

Second, reaching the exit is punished with immediate screen death, as long as there are coloured stones somewhere on the screen.

Third, the path to the exit usually leads inevitably over a large number of these tokens, which must then be cleared out of the way in order to reach it.

So far - well, this game shouldn't cause any problems, you might think now. Not at all, as I would like to say. . . .

The crux is that your ball can only remove a piece from the screen if it is the same colour as the stone to be removed.

Humanly, at PRIDE there is the possibility to recolour the ball as needed, using paint buckets, which are shown here as normal coloured stones with an ornate decoration.

However, these paint buckets can only be used once in each level, after this use they dissolve in air.

This is also the real difficulty of PRIDE. Since you can no longer colour the ball back into a certain colour, you should think carefully about which colour to start with - if you have a choice.

174329.overview: A single player educational game that teaches about prime numbers. Created by Stepping Stone Software for Spinnaker in 1985.

174330.overview: A throwback to a simpler time. LOL. This is Pong, with fun, colorful graphics.

174341.overview: Prison Break: The Text Adventure Game! You have made a bet with a millionaire to escape from a prison.

174342.overview:
Pro Golf is a golf simulator for 1 - 4 players for multiple systems.

Based upon 18 famous holes throughout the world, at the beginning of each hole the player receives a description of the real world course. The game allows a roster of players to be created to allow a player to track their scores over time. At the beginning of each hole the player is informed of wind conditions, and whether the course is wet or dry, and the condition of the greens. The player uses text control to set which club and the power they wish to use. They then set the angle of their shot, and hit the ball. Putting consists of a close up view of the green. The player must avoid trees, water, and sand traps. The gain automatically keeps score.

174343.overview: A simple golf game for up to four players, created by George Adams and published by BMB Compuscience Canada.

174362.overview: A homebrew hockey management game from Chris R. Bickford III and released in 1989.

174364.overview:
A short platform game released in 1988 by 21st Century Software and programmed by Steve Skillcorn. 1997: the Lunar suface-for seven arduous years experts from twelve independent nations have worked feverishly to perfect the P.R.O.B.E. (the Programmable Robot Operated Battle Entity). An awesome weapon of mass destruction, with an intelligence never before anticipated. Six months ago, succeeding completion it was vacated to perform its solitary tasks of protecting the galaxy. But it has turned on mankind and set the time on the doomsday clock. Can you stop it in time?!! 
 
Published in the ECP Gold Ribbon Game Pak.

174392.overview:
A gambling duo that contains "Banco - The Game of Baccarat" & "Draw Poker". 

1. Baccarat
Only the click of chips is missing from this computer version of the popular card game-Baccarat. Beautiful graphic images heighten the excitement of this challenging game.
Unsure of the rules? The rules are built right in! You'll need quick wits to outguess the computer and build a winning hand. Getting nine points may be the hardest thing you have ever done! 

2. Draw Poker
It's Saturday night and the stakes are high. Through the smokey haze, light glimmers off the screen. Sitting across from you is the toughest dealer in town - your computer. It's been said that poker is a game of skill. Here's your chance to prove it! You'll start with $5,000. Try to break the bank and walk away a winner. And remember - no aces up your sleeve in this game!

174393.overview:
A motorcycle racing game mixed with a helping of management simulation game published in Italy as Speedy in Sport Games Nuova Serie n.3 (1993) and by ET software in Europe a few years later. 

Experience the thrill of being in charge of a great speedway team. At the beginning you have to choose which team to lead and you will be immediately introduced to the particular knockout cup at the best of two matches plus a possible play-off. In this competition you have to face an opposing team over the course of 15 races per match. The meetings will take place alternately at home and away. In each race there are 2 riders per team who will get a score (from 4 to 0 points according to the order of arrival) and in the end the one who has obtained the most points wins. Your task is to select the drivers who will make up the starting grid by deciding on the basis of the results obtained by each member of the team (constantly shown on the screen) and also on the basis of opponents. You must be particularly careful not to over-tire your athletes by always having the same riders race!

174396.overview: Let your computer teach you professional magic, or at least some tricks that can be easily translated into simple graphics and presentation.

174402.overview: In the 22nd Century, the Kansler and his spacefleet is about to take over the solar system. An average Joe is captured and remade into the powerful cyborg Argus, to fight the interplanetary war for the Kansler... until he rebels against his masters. Argus and his female counterpart Venix must fight their way across the solar system to win freedom, and end the Kansler's power grab...

174403.overview:
Control your Hell-Storm attack helicopter through levels of underground peril in this horizontally scrolling shoot'em up published in Magic Disk 64 1989/05. 

What disaster has befallen mankind! Lord Rübe robbed all breweries around the world in a night and fog action and carried the beer supplies into his underground cave labyrinth. Should mankind from now on eke out its existence with a dry throat? Will Walter Sedlmaier be robbed of the strong beer tapping and the Paulan acquisition, unemployed? Does Werner only have a chance of "Tass' Kaff '" or "Glass Wass'"? And what about the editorial team of Magic Disk (rattle!)? 

But the rescue seems to be near: Prof. Tom has developed the mega helicopter HELLSTORM (double laser, air rocket, beer sensor, CD player, Playboy collection...) And is now entrusting his old friend and warrior KILLERBYTE with the procurement of the delicious liquid. You are KILLERBYTE (ha, surprise! You probably didn't expect that. . .)! Save humanity from doom!

There are several rules for the game:

MAIN RULE 1: When KILLERBYTE kills, there will be a PILS soon!
MAIN RULE 2: You have three beers. . . uh, three lives!
MAIN RULE 3: Collisions with Lord Turnip's minions and the walls of the cave system lead to the loss of a life!

"Lord Turnip's henchmen?" You will surely ask yourself now. Yes, the underground caves and the secret beer hiding place are guarded by Lord Rübe's guards. These guards immediately go on a collision course if KILLERBYTE approaches in his helicopter.
Every now and then Lord Rübe's robbery squad lost a couple of barrels of beer on the way to the secret hiding place. These barrels in the form of a flashing star need to be collected, because the ingenious Prof. Tom designed his helicopter in such a way that the beer barrel is converted into additional drive and laser energy. If the scrolling suddenly stops, this is not a program error, but something that will make you happy: You have (in fact and contrary to expectations) almost (!) Reached the next level! What now? Just fly out of the right edge of the screen and you are one coaster closer to the beer supply. . .

174407.overview: You are prospecting for gold in the outback goldfields. Move and listen to your metal detector to tell you when you are close to the gold. If you hear a warning signal that means you are near quicksand. Beware of the bushrangers who will spring from nowhere and attack you. Be quick to escape them. Enter the tunnels from the front to travel quickly across the goldfields.

174408.overview: You step down from the stagecoach, tired and dusty, For four days you've been thinking of nothing else but the mine (left to you by your old friend Jake). The stage drives off in a cloud of dust, leaving you standing in the middle of a small Arizona township.

174409.overview: An alien mothership looms above the Earth's surface, dropping deadly alien mines. It is up to you, the cybernetic hero, Protectiod (Half man, half machine) to fly through the earth and blast those deadly mines. Collect power ups to gain more ability to attack those alien mines. There is a protective shield, but sadly that will not last an eternity, because if a mine hits it, the shield gets weakened. Defend your city and avoid contact with those mines. Released for the Minigame Competition 2005 - 4K Category.

174445.overview: A collection of commodore  art created by Talented Design and released in 1991. Not much game here, but quite a bit of cool art. Difficult to believe this was distributed by Virgin Games, especially because of the last bit of art on the it, which is for mature audiences.

174446.overview: A horizontally scrolling shoot'em up game of the "Cassette 50" collection.

174447.overview: Published in Game On 1993/07. An original idea. Move your ship up/down, right to shoot, left to select puzzle piece, and fire to select/throw it. One out of seven pieces is the right match and you can't run out of them, only die if the enemies hit you.

174448.overview:
An adventure game with graphics published in Happy Computer 1985/08, 64'er Sonderheft 66. The game was released in German only, but English language support has unofficially been added to most of the versions in the wild.
 
You have to make the impenetrable walls of Castle Towerhill vanish by magical power.

Versions of this game are available for both German and English.

174449.overview: Drop bombs on to boats. Score as many points as you can before time is out.

174450.overview: A text adventure set in the place where magic and psychology meet.

174451.overview: The final game in the trilogy of text adventures set in the place where magic and psychology meet.

174452.overview:
This game was released on Loadstar #115 in 1993 where it was the winner of the Loadstar programming contest. Touted as a clever joystick game with 24 levels.  Psycloid is a blend of arcade and puzzle game styles. Your goal is to collect all of the energy pods on a level before the time reaches zero and your craft self-destructs. This isn't as tough as it sounds. It's TOUGHER because there are little drones everywhere that want to get you. The levels are rough, but all solvable IF you can find the right strategy.  
 
Your pyramid-shaped craft can move in 4 directions and has a single-shot cannot. You can only fire upwards. The diamond shaped energy pods are collected by touching them with your craft. The round enemy drones are ever present and your craft will be destroyed if it touches one. There are 2 species of drone. The Dormant drone cannot move, but is still deadly to the touch. The Mobile Drone is constantly swarming, only changing directions when it collides with another drone.  
 
The countdown timer will be bumped up by one second when a drone is shot, so it's good idea to shoot as many as possible. There can be over 100 Mobile Drones per level. The hourglass shaped homing mine is intelligent and can travel through walls but not drones. It is indestructible and will attack your craft constantly. There can be up to 4 homing mines per level.

174453.overview:
This great game by Alf Yngve was part of the original Psytronik Software line-up and was due to be released in 1994. Unfortunately the planned enhancements for the game did not happen and the game was not released - UNTIL NOW! Richard Bayliss has continued the project and has delivered this fantastic enhanced version of Psykozone! The game now features a separate intro sequence (complete with digi-tune by FeekZoid), brand new front-end and extra enhancements including 'get ready' and 'game over' sequences + a cool in-game tune by Matt Simmonds (a rendition of the classic theme from 'Streethawk').

Story:
In the twenty first century the United States have collapsed into a myriad of independent regions. Some trade is being made between the regions by using a badly kept net of expressways known as the PSYKOZONE. 

These stretches of road are practically lawless, ruled by gangs of road warriors and genetically-enhanced psycho-bikers. The object of the game is to reach the Pacific ocean by travelling through the most dangerous part of the Psykozone. 

So load up with ammo, oil your engine, fill up your tank, secure the plutonium rods and brake for no-one!

174454.overview: A high quality game created with SEUCK, a vertically scrolling space shooter published in Game On 1988/11, Digital Marketing PD #088, and in Stonysoft #0089.

174455.overview: In the game you must answer 10 multiple-choice questions from a total of 400 questions. These type of games are played in many bars and pubs.

174456.overview: A Pac-Man clone published in 64'er 1992/12. In this version there is no ghost home area and not cross-maze tunnels. Ghosts spawn from other ghosts or from the center of the map.

174457.overview: A Christmas nightmare has begun. Guide your fairy through thin air, avoiding collision with those flying Christmas puds. Get hit by a pud, you lose some energy. Once all your energy is lost, the game is over. Published in GO64! 2002/11.

174458.overview: A minimalist shooter but has good strategic gameplay. Lots of ladders and ways to sneak up on your enemies. Published in Commodore Format 1994/04 (Issue #43).

174459.overview: Vs. your friend! A head-to-head shooter where two players duel for supremacy. Published in Game On 1990/09.

174460.overview:
Avoid the tanks and bulldozers and keep the snakes from growing out of control. 
Night falls, and I'm taken by sleep, hot air blows up balloons in my dreams, Ding-dong!! rings the bell and something's at the door, So I put on my slippers and I creep across the floor. 

For the door from hence I heard, another ding-dong, I peep through the door hole but something's very wrong as on my porch there are thousands of snakes ready to strike, I feel queasy, and my knees start to shake. 

My perilous fate, I see no escape as serpents lay siege to my country estate. The Devil must have opened up hell's gates and called up millions of snakes to take me from this place. 

Big ones Little ones, fat ones skinny ones. Protect me from their venomous drug. That springs from the needles of fangs... Attacked by Snakes

By Snakes!
So many snakes, you could fill the Great Lakes with snakes. Ha ha ha, run. I try to hide. But snake bites on my face testify I've been attacked by snakes. By snakes! So many snakes, it would take a thousand crates to contain the snakes after me. I'd rather be burned at the stake than be... attacked by snakes. 

Welcome to my world, or should I say this land of snakes. Serpents lie and wait at every take, my knees quake as my life these snakes invade.
Snake invaders show their fangs on the snake parade. My perilous fate, I see no escape as my family prays and waits I fight them off with shovels and rakes and bats and phones, but I just can't seem to shake these bones. That slither from the dark to destroy my home. 

One snake, Two snake, are there any more? There's two more knocking at my door...

174461.overview: A game that helps to teach punctuation. Full stop.

174510.overview: An Italian platform game that consists of 24 sequential screens where you have to move your character, a nice puppy, using the joystick in port 2. In each screen you have to eat 10 fruits distributed on the floors of a house connected by ladders. Jump to avoid holes. Your enemies are 4 little birds that move horizontally. You can avoid them by ducking. Snakes and balls popping out from holes can be avoided by jumping over them. Note that snakes can slither at double speed.

174511.overview: Published in the German game magazine, Game On 1991/04 and also included on "Kangarudy II". Your task in this horizontal shooter is to get the ball to a higher level. To shoot you must release the ball, you can catch it again by touching it and holding the button. You only have a certain number of bounces before you lose. So you must let it bounce to destroy the enemies and then grab it up again. The ball shows up on your RADAR in case you get caught up in a battle. You can reach a higher level by entering all of the zones marked by a cross in the lower left display. Some opponents will grab up your ball and take it far away.

174512.overview: Pure-Stat College Basketball is a sports simulation that allows you to replay individual games or entire basketball seasons, from the past or present, while keeping a permanent record of your team's stats using the built in Stat Compiler. In this simulation, you can re-live the excitement of the UCLA teams from the 1960's through the teams of the 80's. The game features 20 "all-time great" teams (as of 1987). Game play features 5 on 5 games across three game modes, 1 on 1, 1 vs CPU, and CPU vs CPU.
