The stat compiler was fairly robust for the time period and tracks steals, blocked shots, assist, rebounds, field goal percentage, foul shot percentage, and time played. The game has managerial aspects to it in that you choose your offensive or defensive play, and then let the computer figure out the play. There was an optional team/trade players disk as well.

174513.overview: Published in Homecomputer 1986/04-05 and a game of "The Big 100" collection. In this I'm an orange box pushing yellow boxes with blue pods trying to kill me.

174514.overview: A puzzle game by Chrlstopher Glaubwitz published in both 64'er 1990/09, and 64'er Sonderheft 79. He has written a nice strategy game, which looks pretty easy at first glance, but has some difficulties. Please type it with the new MSE (Listing 2) After the start you will see a house with 28 cleverly placed boxes. The main character of the game appears on the top left of the screen and can be brought to life with the joystick in port 2. All crates are now to be pushed to the exit. If you finally manage to do this, the game is finished!

174583.overview:
A puzzle game by Frederic Thiesse and published in 64'er Sonderheft 49, and in 64'er Sonderheft 73. The moving of (Boxes in reserved spaces is a strenuous job, especially when you can only move boxes that have free space next to them. You need skill, overview and, above all, the right strategy when you're at "Push'em " don't want to block the way. Once you've got a playing field in order, another 15 parking spaces are waiting for you. With an editor, you can design additional fields according to your wishes, so that your fun can be expanded as you like. Fizzy synthesizer sounds provide a suitable background music this exciting strategy task.

 You control the robot, which is represented by a silver ball, with a joystick in port 2. You can also see the storage area with green, square boxes and the parking spaces provided for them, which are marked by blue hollows in the ground. Your robot's task is to transport the green boxes into these hollows. To do this first place the robot ball directly next to a box. Then the fire button is pressed and the joystick is moved in the direction of the crate. Always place the robot on the opposite side to which you want to move the box. If a box is to be “pushed” more than one spot, the fire button must be pressed for each movement to be carried out. However, the robot can only move one box at a time; if there are two or more boxes, his power fails. If a crate is on one of the parking spaces, it turns blue. It can also be moved away from there and thus once again assume the green or blue color. At the bottom of the playing field, two counters indicate the number of your robot movements (»MOVES«) and box displacements (»PUSHES«). It is thus possible for experts to determine optimal strategies, i.e. the most economical ways possible. 

The main difficulty with this task is that it is very easy to get into a dead end situation, such as when you have maneuvered a box into a corner or blocked your own way. In this situation, only the emergency brake F7 helps, with which you can abort the game and go back to the beginning. A playing field is completely drawn when there are no more green boxes or no more parking spaces. Then it continues with the crates in the next of the 16 levels.

174587.overview: Who can finish the 5x5 slide-puzzle first. A head-to-head duel of the puzzlemasters. Published in Game On 1994/07.

174588.overview: A single player puzzle game with music by Gösta Feiweier. Published in 1993 by Digital Express.

174623.overview:
Puzzlacki is a classic puzzle game with 8 available pictures. The player may setup difficulty level and timer or select any of the pictures. The game screen is divided into three parts: table with mixed puzzles, timer, picture frame. Published on Magic Disk 64 1994/09. Do you enjoy solving a puzzle?

Well, then Puzzlacki is definitely the right thing for you! After starting the program, the following options can be selected:

•   infinite time
•   Simplified game mode
•   background music

You also have to choose one of the numerous puzzle pictures:

This is done with the joystick in port # 2. Then get down to business. You can activate a puzzle piece with the fire button and switch to the picture to be completed with SPACE. Here you can now place the selected part according to your ideas. You come back to the end of the puzzle with SPACE.
If you know all the puzzles like the back of your hand after a while, you can try the expert mode or set yourself a strict time limit. The choice is yours!

174624.overview: You will be presented with the Incan Gate and one of the 9 sections does not match the pattern, find it quickly and you can proceed on your journey, fail to find it in time and your journey is over.

174625.overview: An electronic version of a 25 piece sliding Gem Puzzle\Mystic Square where you put all the numbered pieces back in order to rebuild a larger overall picture.

174626.overview: A puzzle game created by  Dave Hogendorf and Patrick Witteman and published in Golden Disk 64 #11 (1990). The puzzle game for bright minds and quick combiners. A game against time! After starting through the main menu you get directly into the game. The computer then immediately mixes the individual building blocks of the graphic in the upper right corner. Now you have to try to restore the original picture by moving the parts of the picture in as few moves as possible. To do this, use the joystick. The display on the left shows the time remaining, as well as the number of points achieved and the high score

174643.overview: Published in 64'er Sonderheft 97, this game is a jigsaw puzzle of sorts. You're given all the pieces to make the puzzle and you must lock them into the right locations to increase your score and complete the overall picture.

174644.overview: A popular single player puzzle and strategy game created by Michael Pietrzak and Olaf Peters and published in 64'er 1991/03, 64'er Sonderheft 79, and 64'er 1998/05.

174646.overview: Somewhere in this vast desert is the Lost Tomb of Rak-Tuman and all his treasure. Many men have set out to become rich but none have returned with few actually reaching the pyramid itself. You are one such treasure hunter, and with a map you set off towards The Pyramid but be careful as it's easy to get lost in the desert. If you make it there will be puzzles, traps and creatures waiting for you. The Pyramid is a text adventure where text describes each location and you type commands with the keyboard to control your hero and interact with each location.

174648.overview: Pyramid Pete is a 3D puzzle platformer in the vein of Q-bert made by Mike Platt and Published in Italy in the Go Games n.10 (June 1986). It was originally  published by Alpha Software in 1984.

174649.overview:
Pyramid Puzzler is a 1 - 2 player game designed to teach multiplication.

Two players attempt to reach the top of a pyramid by correctly answering multiplication questions. There are 3 levels of question difficulty., and each player gets 10 seconds to correctly answer a question. If they are successful, they get to move 1 position. If they answer incorrectly, their opponent gets to move 2 positions. If two players land on the same position, the player who was there first gets a chance to answer another question. If they are correct, their opponent is bounced backwards, otherwise they are bumped backwards.

174651.overview: A simple adventure game with RPG elements. You have entered the desert of Lost Sands and traveled to the Pyramid of Pyro. Your mission is to gain as much experience as you can and bring back the Eternal Flame, one of Pyro's prized possessions. There are 10 levels to the pyramid but you can leave any time you please.

176485.overview: Professional Lode Runner is a special version of the Lode Runner 1 disk version, with which you can create an own executable game set and some additional levels for play.

177283.overview:
This is like something between Lode Runner and the Atari 2600 version of The Sorceror's Apprentice. The objective is to switch off all the taps before the place is flooded. 

This was dveloped by Alain Tremblay and published as a type-in by COMPUTE! Publications, Inc. in the 1992/04 issue of COMPUTE!'s Gazette (which was at the time an insert in the regular COMPUTE! magazine, and not a standalone magazine)

177672.overview: This family game is based on 4 different motifs that have to be put together correctly. Decisive are the 5 levels of difficulty, which break down the overall puzzle picture into more and more individual parts. Long-lasting fun for everyone!

177829.overview: A relatively simple pool game from Abacus Software, later it would be released in Jim Green PD #04.

178395.overview: Flipper pinball game by Antti Kyllönen and Jarmo Nikula published in MikroBitti Magazine Issue 1988/01.

178623.overview:
Professional Boulder Dash is a 1985 Rom Hack of Boulder Dash III with edited levels and faster gameplay. It was modified by Sijben Soft. Published in Italy as Roc in Super Game 2000 n.10 (Dicembre 1985) and in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - super top (1986). 

Rocford aka Roc, the lovable hero of the game, must recover all the diamonds found in the Silicen mine. The collection of gems is very dangerous ass the mine, which has been abandoned for centuries, is subject to landslides produced by every slightest movement. The quarries of the mine are populated by strange forms of life: the prolific green amoebas and the frenetic butterflies. These beings with particular precautions can be transformed into precious diamonds. Amoebas must be surrounded by boulders to prevent their continuous development while butterflies crushed by boulders will expose a diamond for the taking. Beware of terrible and deadly electric quadropolises that, released from their cells, will chase and disintegrate you. The riches of this mine are at your disposal but it will not be easy to take possession of them.

178971.overview:
Here is another work from the Sputnik World group. Panzer , a game halfway between arcade and military strategy based on the PC classic "Codename: Panzers". A development that shows us an approximation of this title for the Commodore 64 .

Panzer, short for the name Panzerkampfwagen, whose German meaning means "armored fighting vehicle." Refers to German tanks from World War II. Under this concept and inspired by its namesake for PC Sputnik World presents its new game. 

The objective of the game will be to take control of the four camps that exist in the battle area, receiving a Medal for each one that we manage to control.

This circumstance creates in the player an exploration effect in the first games to discover the elements it contains and plan how to approach the strategy to complete the mission successfully.

179007.overview: Prime Maze is an educational math game developed by A.T. Webber and L.T Webber and published by Australian based company EDU-KIT Productions. In 1983. The game is also playable on the VIC-20 using a memory expansion.

179330.overview:
Compilation including the following three Popeye games:

Popeye
Popeye 2
Popeye 3: WrestleCrazy

179430.overview:
An early version of Hero of the Golden Talisman, which is quite a bit different, featuring different music, screens, enemies and a rather bizarre swimming animation! It was leaked to the scene and has been floating around under a number of different pseudonyms including "Labyrinth" and "Progfine" at one point.
 
Published in Italy as Minaccia al Mondo in Logica 2000 n.18 (Marzo 1986).

180500.overview: A fantastic compilation of all the things a Pac-Maniac needs. Originally released at the Excess & Abyss Connection Party 2020. Supports both PAL and NTSC.

180546.overview: Released at the Commodoremania 2016 Compo and placing sixth in the Mixed Game Competition there. This outstanding set of 5 pinball tables, created with the Pinball Construction Set are somehow crammed into a single disk.

180547.overview: A head to head vs shooting game for 2 players. It was released at Datastorm 2018, in Sweden.

180557.overview: A trivia/quiz game where points are awarded in the form of dollars for each correct question, the goal was to reach a high schore of $10,000 with questions ranging awards related to the difficulty. Published in RUN 1988/11 (Issue #59).

180595.overview: A version of Pinball Wizard created using the Pinball Construction Set and released by Gonzo Weird (GZW) in response to the Sagittarian version. The intent was to make a game that was more in line with the far superior Amiga version of the game.

180596.overview: A pinball table created with the Pinball Construction Set by DAG. Not sure if DAG was a poor speller or if the name refers to a group or BBS. But it has some nice pirate themed play and a super score for lighting all entryway lights.

180606.overview: Known as both 4 Aces Pinball and Poker of Aces, this pinball table, created with the Pinball Construction Set features a playing card motif. Score more points that your opponent or exceeding your personal best is the goal of this game. It is up to you to keep the ball in the field by bouncing it against the buffers and hitting the targets to score as many points as possible. Try to send the ball into the side corridor where the word POKER appears, to ear bonus points and hit as many targets as possible before you lose all 5 balls. Published in Italy as Poker D'Assi in the Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - mega collection (1985).

180607.overview: A pinball table created by Joshua Derocher using the Pinball Construction Set and published in Loadstar #199.

180608.overview: the best caves from Rockford's Super Boulder and New CAves from Rockford. Rockford * Rockford!

180609.overview: The final release in this collection of increasingly difficult levels where you must determine how to get all the diamonds from the level without being trapped, squashed, caught by monsters or running out of time.

180610.overview:
A game created by Giuseppe Vollara aka VG Vox ak Pinov Vox for the 2019 SEUCK Compo. It is the Year 2325 ...

The protagonist Captain John Rostar catapulted into a parallel universe in a hostile world dominated by technology and strange aliens and giant animals that resemble giant reptiles. The Captain must command a fleet of spacecraft and defeat and rescue two important Androids to leave this parallel universe.

Find the 2 friends of your friends and defeat the aliens and monsters of the PROTOX1 planet.

180611.overview: Puralax is a simple puzzle game where you need to paint every colored tile into one single color to complete each level. Each level has a different target color, indicated by the color of the top bar on the screen.

180612.overview: More new levels for you Push'Em puzzlers! Also known as Mic's Push' Em.

180717.overview: An action game, created by Michael Balle and published in 64'er Software Extra Nr.10: Spiele - Volume 3.

181951.overview: A conversion of the game for the PET\CBM computer that was originally created in 2017. Converted by "Who Cares" all credits and attributions go to the original creators.

181989.overview:
A crosshairs tank shooter that was released as part of "Arcade Games" pack and in 1984, COMPUTE!'s Gazette/COMPUTE! Publications, Inc.  as Supertank. Additionally it was part of COMPUTE!'s Third Book of Commodore 64.

The game also got translations to Dutch, French and Italian. 

The Dutch version was published by Holt, Rinehart and Winston Ltd. as a type-in listing from the book "16 voor de 64"

Also released in Italy in the following: Super VIC & C64 A2-N04 (April 1985), Jackson Soft Compilation #4

183636.overview: Puck-Man is an obvious clone of Namco's Pac-Man, although using the original Japanese early release name. It was developed by Claus Mayer in 1983

185669.overview: Guide the parachutist onto the base at the bottom of the screen. He is only moveable when the chute is open. Push the button to jump from the plane and pull the joystick back to pop your canopy. Watch the wind indicator, they can be fierce around here. Game of the "Cassette 50" collection.

189898.overview: A puzzle/arcade game heavily inspired by Lemmings for the immortal C64! Planet Balls was inhabited by peaceful balls that lived under the guidance of their King. But one bad day the evil Dark Cube made them all prisoners! Save King Ball and his subjects and restore peace on the planet! Planet Balls is reminiscent of Lemmings but in a more light way. Your ball buddies have a start point and the goal is to reach the end point without losing any. You can build blocks over each other to make the Balls reach there destination. You get some obstacles, blocks that cannot build, blocks that remove... so it got more and more difficult at each level.

190946.overview: A Pengo style arcade action game published in ECP's "Gold Ribbon Game Pak".

191251.overview: In Picture Parts, children complete a series of math problems to gain familiarity with fundamental math computation skills. Children create pictures as they solve addition, subtraction, and multiplication problems. The program has 3 levels of difficulty; by the time children have made every possible picture combination, they will have spent hours practicing the most important basic math skills. Ages 4-8.

192172.overview: Paul's Gamble Machine is a 2017  gambling/slot machine game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Paul van der Laak and released into the public domain.

192402.overview: A shoot'em up game published in  the book "Commodore 64 Assembly Language Arcade Game Programming" and in the Italian magazine Go Games n.4 (December 1985) as Phoenix.

192428.overview:
Piloting a landing module, you must disengage from the support spaceship and attempt a soft landing on the planet Zombi. The module is equipped with small thrusters that you will need to use to mitigate the descent and to land safely on the ramp that will appear on the screen. Instrumentation on-board will report all the parameter which you will need to take into account. 

Published in Italy as Pilota Astrale in Go Games n.10 (Giugno 1986) and in Super Game 2000 N°10 (Dicembre 1985) as Recupera i Cristalli.

192648.overview: The Potion is a short text adventure developed by Peter Karlsson of Softwolves  for the 2003 Mini-Game Competition in the 4K category. The game object is to mix the potion with salt water.

192932.overview: Pong Machine is a single player only Pong clone for the Commodore 64. This one was developed by Jörg Heyltjes of Technische Maschinenfabrik in 2010 and released into the public domain. It was loosely based on the rare early Pong Machines that Commodore themselves produced in the late 70s.

192945.overview:
Planet X2.1 is an enhanced version of David "8-Bit Guy" Murray's 2017 C64 Real-Time Strategy/Role-Playing  game Planet X2. The game has some graphical enhancements over the original game. Basically a "remastered" version of the original game.

Also Unlike the original version, this version is available as a digital download, and also on cartridge.

This version was released on October 25, 2020.

The game is compatible on both PAL and NTSC C64s.

193518.overview: Pocket Dungeon is an action adventure with RPG elements. It was developed by Georg "Endurion" Rottensteiner with graphics done by his wife, Emily, for the RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2019. A little procedural dungeon romp. Delve into the dungeons, fight monsters to gain levels and find out what it takes to gather the relic and escape!

195671.overview: A SEUCK shooter created by Dr. Ice of IRS. featuring 2 player simultaneous, cooperative play. The Xenians are a people who represent a constant danger to the interstellar Federation. In fact, they continue to make border rids, attacking numerous convoys. The Federation has, of course, tried several times to attack the Xenian post but unfortunately always without success. They are perched inside the planet Xenia, whose entrance consists of a very narrow and also very well defended tunnel. Many pilots have already given up their lives and therefor the Federation has decided to suspend any further attacks. This does not mean that he will remain and watch: in fact he has developed a simulator on which to train the pilots and only hose who manage to pass this extremely difficult test will have th honor of attempting to defeat the Xenians!

196061.overview: Enter the tomb and be prepared to fight bats, beetles, snakes and traps galore. Watch the bats! They'll push you around. Published in Commodore 64 Club #01 [Italian Release].

196900.overview: BrainWave is a free puzzle game inspired by Mahjong tile removal games, the main difference being the setting and the design of the pieces. it was released in Italy under several names including Double Box, Pezzo Doppio and Piramix.

199637.overview: A brain/memory game for 1 to 10 people created by James Midgley & John van Ness and published by Micro Spec and by Suncom as part of the "Suncom Six Pack Plus". Published in Italy in Computing videoteca Nuova serie - Giochi Di Società 2 (giugno 1986).

200004.overview: A ROM hack created by Zenmaster where the Petch\Pengo game's speed was doubled for a faster and more challenging game.

200164.overview: PETSCII-Poker is a single player computerized poker game for the Commodore 64. The game uses nothing but PETSCII graphics, hence the name. It was developed by Software of Sweden and released into the public domain in 2015. There is also a demo mode in which you can see the AI against itself.

200906.overview: Not to be confused with 1984 "Plumb Crazy!", Plumb Crazy is a remake of its namesake for Atari ST. The game is a take of the classic puzzler Pipe Dream. Your goal is to construct a large enough network of pipes before the time runs out and the water starts to flow. The game was released in both Loadstar #154, and in the fourth from the last Loadstar #247 in 2007.

201452.overview:
Parkering (also known as The Parking Game) is a 1987 C64 game developed by Simon Fox and published under the label "Silent Soft" This game was the only C64 game that both Fox and Silent Soft released, which may have been just a personal label used by Fox.

The objective of this game is to park your car in-between other cars without 1. passing the cars 2. crashing into the cars or the side of the road.

The game sounds simple enough, but it's not as easy as it looks.

Getting the game started is slightly tricky, however. First off when you run the game, and the crackscreen comes up, you have to press the fireb utton on the port 2 joystick, then once the crackscreen ends, and the official title screen appears, you then have to switch to port 1, as the game plays using port 1 and not port 2. Then in order to start the game, you MUST read the instructions, as simply pressing the fire button does not actually work. Then once you read the instructions, you then have to press F7 to start the game. 
 
Released in Italy in the Alga Soft n.19a compilation.

202283.overview: Pro Keno is a Keno simulation developed by Ron Doty. The year of release is not currently known

202628.overview: It is a hard life for the friendly forest dwellers! The Smurfette is lost and a villager needs to go find her and bring her back safely home. The game consists of a long path full of pitfalls and obstacles that you must avoid and overcome only by dodging and jumping. You will meet many animals that you absolutely must not touch, or lose one of your three lives. You will have to move, even in the creepy darkness.

206654.overview:
A simple adventure game for kids with selectable answers. First published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/08 (Issue #38),  in COMPUTE!'s Commodore 64/128 Collection - Volume 2 and then as part of Australia's "Red Pack" published by Street games. Modified versions were later released in Jim Green PD Disk #31, and in Q-Link #57.  
 
Children can enter a swashbuckling world of pirates as they attempt to find Treasure Island and the treasure chest in this mini adventure. While providing entertainment and challenge, it also sharpens map -reading and direction skills. 
 
In "Pirate Cove" your child plays the role of a buccaneer who's found a map showing the locations of ten Islands, Starting from Pirate Cove, he or she must navigate around the territory trying to find Treasure Island, Along the way, the child 
may find Spice Island, Mermaid's Lagoon,- or Skeleton Island, among others. Also, the child may search sunken ships or fight the Sea Monster, The game is over when Treasure Island has been found and the treasure chest successfully opened.

206662.overview:
Published first in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1985/11 (Issue #29), Then in Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette, and also in COMPUTE!'s Third Book of C64 Games. It was published under the same name by Macrisoft a year later in Spain, though the gameplay is in English. At some point Corbois Software published this in Dutch.  This is one of the most addictive games we've ever published. It adds a new dimension to the traditional game of poker, and is fun for one player or in competition with friends.

Poker is a game that's just as popular today as it was a century ago. Even though there's always a random element at play, it usually requires careful thought and a 
knowledge of probability, The variations created by the cards you're dealt and how you arrange them makes poker unpredictable, "Power Poker," written for the Commodore 64, adds a new twist to the game — rather, another dimension. 

Think of this game as two-dimensional poker. You play on a five-by-five grid and try to make the hands that gain the most points. Each card serves two hands, so 
placement must be done carefully,

206716.overview:
Prisonball is a two-player action game that combines the best elements from two classic computer games, Pong and Breakout. The object of the game is simple — knock out as many bricks as you can in the allotted time. 

The game begins by displaying five colored walls running vertically down the center of the screen. Each player controls two paddles located at the left and right sides of the screen. Three balls appear at a random location and start bouncing around the screen. When a ball is on your side of the screen, move one of your paddles into its path to deflect the ball toward the walls. If you happen to miss a ball, it wraps around the screen and appears on
the other side, giving your opponent a chance to score.

At the beginning of the game, all three balls are a neutral color. Each time you hit a ball, it changes to the color of your paddle. You score whenever a ball of your color hits one of the five interior walls.

First published in COMPUTE! 1986/10 (Issue #77), and later in Best of COMPUTE! & Gazette.

208298.overview:
Price of Peril is a German language text adventure with graphics for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Michael B. Schmidt and published in Input 64  1988/04. There are enough science fiction novels and films out there, but have you ever projected yourself into the future? It's possible with a sci-fi adventure. Put yourself in the shoes of the hunted. You will be hounded and pursued throughout the city. You are exhausted and can't take it anymore, it's over. Your pursuers have caught up with you, a shot is fired — you can actually feel yourself sinking to the ground. But then the door opens: “Come on, dinner is ready” — you breathe a sigh of relief, it was just a game: Price of Peril.
 
The year is 2013. Four years ago voluntary suicide became legal. However, this innovation, which initially appears harmless, is being unscrupulously exploited by the media by putting on television shows in which the individual candidates risk their lives. Jim Raeder also lived during this time. He has never been very successful professionally and is persuaded by a friend to take part in such a program. The television company takes an interest in Jim and initially lets him act in a few small shows in which, apart from a few injuries, he is more or less successful. But then comes the big breakthrough for Jim. He gets an offer to take part in the most popular gladiator game of modern times: Price of Peril. In this game you are hunted by one of the worst crime gangs in New York. If the criminals succeed in killing the candidate, they will be pardoned by the government. The contestant wins if he survives the predetermined time limit. The hunt is broadcast live on television using cameras installed in helicopters. The show will be hosted by the very popular Mike Terry. In addition, viewers can take part in the murderous game by calling the broadcaster as so-called "Good Samaritans" and then giving the candidate tips and tricks via television.

208679.overview:
Puzzle Bobble is an unofficial conversion of the Taito arcade classic of the same name, for the Commodore 64. It was released on February 1, 2022. Although, the conversion has been in the works since sometime around mid-2019. 

The conversion was done by a group called JHB. It even allows you to insert credits using the same keys you would use on MAME and even has a version of the classic NEO-GEO green startup screen and splash screen to make it look more authentic.

The game is currently PAL only. Supports keyboard, joystick, and paddles.

Game description:

Puzzle Bobble is a real-time puzzle game in which the player controls a device called "pointer" at the bottom of the screen, aiming and releasing randomly colored bubbles upwards. Depending on the aiming, the bubbles may float up directly or bounce off the walls, changing their trajectory. The goal is to aim the bubbles in such a way that they will touch identically colored ones. When such bubbles form a group of three or more, they pop and disappear from the screen.

If the ceiling of the area is covered by too many bubbles, it will gradually descend; the game is over when it nearly reaches the player-controlled pointer. Should the player fail to release the bubbles within a specific time limit, they will be released automatically, unaffected by the pointer's aiming.

A two-player mode is included as well. Each player competes on an area occupying half of the screen, dealing with identically generated bubbles. Whenever a player successfully disposes of a bubble group, a part of it is transferred onto the opponent's part of the screen.

The game features the two dinosaur protagonists (Bob and Bub) as well as other characters from Bubble Bobble, even though the two games have distinctly different gameplay.

"A high-tech toilet," Andrew reminisces when you ask him where the name Paradroid came from. "That's what Technobots always reminds me of... We were messing around with some names and somehow we came up with Technobots. I even had it on the title screen for a while," he continues. "But then Paradroid came along and saved the day. It's a play on PARAnoid anDROID - everyone's out to get you."

TheOne: Work in Progress - Paradroid '90

Bugs

    Enemy laser 1 / laser 2 damage was swapped.
    fixed
    Rarely droid mode wasn't initialized correctly, making some droids explode when entering level.
    fixed
    Player could go through walls by abusing asymmetry in wall collision check.
    fixed
    Droid exploding simultanously with other events had multiple problems:
        Transfer with such droid resulted in droid 402 (index $40, explosion).
        fixed
        Player droid in multiple collision. This might also lose one of exploding enemy droids.
        fixed
        Player droid bumped off from explosion, thinking it was 402-type droid.
        fixed
    DroidNear() returned true for some faraway droids.
    fixed
    Waypoints had multiple problems too:
        Droids might lose waypoints if bumped into when they were just leaving one. This resulted in droid reversing its direction and going where no droid has gone before.
        fixed
        Droids ignored waypoints if they paused (either they fired or were bumped into) at the exact same time they entered waypoint.
        fixed
        Game checked for waypoints twice as often as necessary. (And how much did it help...)
        fixed
    Non-visible area scanned was different in each direction.
    fixed
    Hardware collision checks are basically crap. Originally game tried to handle this by checking the topmost colliding sprites, ignoring others.
    fixed
    Interrupts didn't clear decimal flag, causing sound corruption every now and then.
    fixed (This was also fixed in the Heavy Metal Paradroid)
    The very last waypoint of the very last deck (maintenance) sent droids to wall.
    fixed
